text.p: General Magic Inc., an Internet software provider, said Wednesday it has cut its workforce to about 138 from about 187 regular and contract workers.

The company, which has been plagued by losses, said the job cuts will help it gain tighter controls over spending and refocus its workforce on the next set of initiatives in its Internet business strategy.
In June, General Magic revamped its futuristic software to turn them into Internet browsing and searching tools.

"This step, although difficult, is necessary for us to sharpen our focus on the company's business strategy and to maintain existing commitments with our partners," said Steve Markman, president and chief executive.
The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based company's stock was unchanged at $1.69 on Nasdaq in late trading.
